selected_text: Hypothesis: the storage path's constant recorded value collapses token entropy, because the lookup returns the stored value, not the key it looked up, and the handler re-uses that value as the validated token; validation therefore accepts a fixed constant that any attacker knows in advance. Prerequisites: default non-single-use configuration with the memory backend, disposable in-process app, fake request interface. Bounded test: first safe request mints a random cookie; replay it on a second safe request and read the rotated cookie value; then send a state-changing request from a completely fresh client with the suspected constant as both the extracted token and the cookie, plus a control state-changing request with an attacker-chosen unknown random value. Expected support: the second safe response rotates the cookie to the constant and the fresh-client constant request is accepted (success status) while the unknown value is rejected. Falsifier: the constant request is rejected or the cookie never collapses. Cleanup: fixtures are disposable; keep the sequence script as the regression core.
